entities.summary: Hans Memling was a German-Flemish painter who worked in the tradition of Early Netherlandish painting. Born in the Middle Rhine region, he probably spent his childhood in Mainz. During his apprenticeship as a painter he moved to the Netherlands and spent time in the Brussels workshop of Rogier van der Weyden. In 1465 he was made a citizen of Bruges, where he became one of the leading artists and the master of a large workshop. A tax document from 1480 lists him among the wealthiest citizens. Memling's religious works often incorporated donor portraits of the clergymen, aristocrats, and burghers who were his patrons.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Hans Memling's paintings often incorporated donor portraits of prominent patrons, reflecting his role as a leading artist in Bruges and his ability to secure wealth for himself through patronage. His workshop produced works that showcased the city's growing artistic influence.
